question: Would giving every newly discoverable sentence encoder a matched, supervised chance improve on the previous ordinary release's protected portfolio? Measure the additional resource both alone and as an optional contributor.
scope: Training-only follow-up. Use exclusively the 6631 rows supplied to the original arm of the Arctic resource experiment. Do not use its 1670 outer rows or labels, any course-designated validation labels, official test, movie holdout or H2. The protected recipe is the exact weights and members of the historical portfolio_revised autonomous election. Its choice was informed by the original full training set; this is a development diagnostic.
partition: Five stratified, shared-text-component folds with shuffle and seed from SHA256('AIAA resource audition separated roles v1') first eight hex characters. Assign folds 0,1,2 to nomination, confirmation and audit. Train each model once on the combined remaining two folds. No supervised preprocessing, model or threshold may fit on the three held roles. The fixed text embeddings may use the already available individual-text cache. Seal all component probabilities before nomination.
menus: All declaratively discovered eligible local Sentence Transformers in the original vs expanded inventories plus the protected recipe. Exactly one production worker fit per unique model, at most ten in total, shared across both menus. Every available encoder is measured even when the ordinary scheduler skipped it. This controlled audition is separate from the unhinted ordinary solve. Immutable encoder signatures break equal scores.
rule: For each menu, freely nominate a single optional encoder and its share from 25%, 50% or 100%, or keep the protected recipe. Maximise nomination accuracy, prefer keeping on a tie, then the smaller nonzero contribution, then the lexical content signature. Lock both choices before reading confirmation scores. Deploy a nominee only if it beats the protected recipe on confirmation; ties keep the existing recipe. Freeze the two final choices before reading audit scores. Report standalone component accuracy, the new encoder's gains/losses at each share against the protected recipe, and the policy's independent audit comparison. Show even negative results.
decision: This experiment can justify a second-domain independent audition only if the expanded policy both actually uses the new encoder and beats the old menu and protected recipe on the audit. Even then require another domain or fresh task before changing the ordinary production policy. No re-selection from audit answers.
budget: At most 10 new local supervised fits, 0 generative-model requests, 0 paid tokens.
